diagram_math_checks.result: The local oriented-graph definition gives o(e)=v and t(e)=w. For e′=h·e the action preserves incidence, so v′=h·v and w′=h·w, as used in the lemma Statement and proof 2.1. The picture shows stabilizer groups, with edge orientation specified in its introductory prose.

Upper horizontal maps are i_v:G_e -> G_v and i_w:G_e -> G_w; lower maps are i_v′:G_e′ -> G_v′ and i_w′:G_e′ -> G_w′. All are inclusions g -> g. Proof 1.1 establishes subgroup containment, so arrows point from each central edge stabilizer to its endpoint stabilizers.
All three downward maps c_h send g to hgh^{-1}, from G_x to G_{h·x}, x=v,e,w. This matches proof 2.1; the inverse is c_{h^{-1}}. No vertical arrow reverses the conjugation direction.

For g in G_e, c_h(i_v(g))=hgh^{-1}=i_v′(c_h(g)) in G_v′, and c_h(i_w(g))=hgh^{-1}=i_w′(c_h(g)) in G_w′. This is exactly the simultaneous conjugacy of the two inclusions in proof 2.1. The original rigorous proof is unchanged and independent of the figure.
